clinical.citation: Jin et al. 2025 - Genomic analysis of 11,555 probands identifies 60 dominant congenital heart disease genes (PMID: 40127276)

variants.description: Damaging de novo mutations in LHX2 (specific variant notation not provided in the text)
phenotypes: Congenital heart disease
Aortic atresia
Mitral atresia

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Significant burden of damaging de novo variants in LHX2 among CHD probands; gene pLI = 0.99; mouse knockouts produce CHD. Both probands with damaging DNMs had aortic and mitral atresia.
clinical.center_country: Pediatric Cardiac Genomics Consortium (PCGC); multicenter, likely USA

model_organism.citation: Shi et al. 1997 (Porter et al.) - Lhx2, a LIM homeobox gene, is required for eye, forebrain, and definitive erythrocyte development (PMID: 9247336)
phenotypes: anophthalmia: optic vesicle specified but eye development arrests before optic cup formation
cerebral cortex malformation with neocortical hypoplasia due to deficient forebrain proliferation
aplasia of hippocampal anlagen
severe anemia from a cell non-autonomous defect in definitive erythropoiesis

model_organism.citation: Monuki et al. 2001 - LIM-homeodomain gene Lhx2 regulates the formation of the cortical hem (PMID: 11165475)
phenotypes: expanded cortical hem covering almost the entire dorsal telencephalon at E12.5
no hippocampal differentiation adjacent to the mutant hem
overall dorsoventral patterning not perturbed
defective early telencephalic patterning

model_organism.citation: Chou & Tole 2009 (Chou et al.) - Lhx2 specifies regional fate in Emx1 lineage of telencephalic progenitors generating cerebral cortex (PMID: 19820705)
phenotypes: Emx1-cre deletion at E10.5 altered progenitor fate
progenitors generated three-layer cortex resembling olfactory cortex instead of lateral neocortex
no ectopic olfactory cortex after deletion at E11.5, indicating a critical period

model_organism.citation: Hsu et al. 2015 - Lhx2 regulates the timing of β-catenin-dependent cortical neurogenesis (PMID: 26371318)
phenotypes: Nestin-cre deletion produced a dramatically smaller cortex
reduced cortical progenitor proliferation
precocious radial glia differentiation and temporal shift of neurogenesis
Wnt/β-catenin pathway failed to maintain progenitor proliferation

model_organism.citation: de Melo et al. 2016 - Lhx2 Is an Essential Factor for Retinal Gliogenesis and Notch Signaling (PMID: 26911688)
phenotypes: failure of Müller glia development at all stages: reduced proliferation of gliocompetent progenitors, loss of Müller-specific gene expression, and impaired terminal differentiation
rapid downregulation of Notch pathway genes (Notch1, Dll1, Dll3, Hes1, Hes5, Sox8, Rax) and loss of Notch signaling
Hes5-induced gliogenesis requires Lhx2

model_organism.citation: Subramanian et al. 2011 - Transcription factor Lhx2 is necessary and sufficient to suppress astrogliogenesis and promote neurogenesis in the developing hippocampus (PMID: 21690374)
phenotypes: Lhx2 disruption by in utero electroporation and in organotypic slice culture caused premature astrocyte production in the hippocampus during the neurogenic period
loss of Lhx2 in neocortex did not cause premature astrogliogenesis

model_organism.citation: Wang et al. 2017 - Lhx2 Expression in Postmitotic Cortical Neurons Initiates Assembly of the Thalamocortical Somatosensory Circuit (PMID: 28122236)
phenotypes: layer 4 barrel cortex neurons initially specified but failed to form cellular barrels or polarized dendrites
thalamocortical axons reached barrel cortex but failed to arborize into barrels
downregulation of activity-regulated and barrel-formation genes including Btbd3 (direct Lhx2 target)

model_organism.citation: Marcos-Mondéjar et al. 2012 - The lhx2 transcription factor controls thalamocortical axonal guidance by specific regulation of robo1 and robo2 receptors (PMID: 22457488)
phenotypes: thalamus-specific Lhx2 deletion produced topographic thalamocortical axon defects, particularly in projections from the medial geniculate nucleus and caudal ventrobasal nucleus
altered Robo1 and Robo2 expression

model_organism.citation: Kim et al. 2014 - Lhx2 regulates bone remodeling in mice by modulating RANKL signaling in osteoclasts (PMID: 24902903)
phenotypes: osteoporotic bone phenotype
increased osteoclast formation in vivo

model_organism.citation: Mardaryev et al. 2006 (Rhee et al.) - Lhx2 maintains stem cell character in hair follicles (PMID: 16809539)
phenotypes: loss-of-function showed Lhx2 maintains growth and undifferentiated properties of hair follicle progenitors
hair follicle stem cell specification and maintenance defects

biological.citation: Lhx2 specifically expressed in HSCs promotes liver regeneration and inhibits liver fibrosis (PMID: 39693275)
biological.summary: Lhx2 is a hepatic stellate cell (HSC)-specific transcription factor that is higher in healthy than fibrotic liver in mouse and human. Knockdown impaired regeneration after acute injury. HSC-specific overexpression promoted hepatocyte proliferation and reduced fibrosis, upregulated SMAD6 to block TGF-β signaling, and acted upstream of pro-regenerative factors such as HGF.

biological.citation: LHX2 Rewires the Metabolic and Epigenetic Landscape to Drive Tumor Progression in Prostate Cancer (PMID: 40899980)
biological.summary: In neuroendocrine prostate cancer models, glycolysis-derived lactate and histone lactylation increase LHX2 expression. LHX2 then transcriptionally activates LDHA, forming a positive feedback loop, and upregulates DNMT1 to drive neuroendocrine gene expression and tumor growth. Paritaprevir binds LHX2 directly and suppresses neuroendocrine markers and tumor progression.

biological.citation: Lhx2 regulates the timing of β-catenin-dependent cortical neurogenesis (PMID: 26371318)
biological.summary: Nestin-Cre deletion of Lhx2 in cortical progenitors produced a much smaller cortex through precocious radial glia differentiation and a temporal shift in neurogenesis. Without Lhx2, Wnt/β-catenin signaling could not maintain progenitor proliferation, so Lhx2 is required for β-catenin function.

biological.citation: Lhx2 regulates the development of the forebrain hem system (PMID: 23307637)
biological.summary: Lhx2 limits the extent of the cortical hem, septum and thalamic eminence. Loss of Lhx2 greatly expands all three structures and dramatically increases the Cajal-Retzius cell population. Lhx2 therefore acts as a central regulator of telencephalic midline patterning.

biological.citation: Mapping the expression of epithelial hair follicle stem cell-related transcription factors LHX2 and SOX9 in the human hair follicle (PMID: 25808706)
biological.summary: In human anagen hair follicles, LHX2 protein is found throughout the outer root sheath, including the bulge. LHX2+ cells are mostly in the sub-bulge and proximal bulb ORS rather than restricted to the bulge. Expression increases in proximal follicle epithelium during catagen, and most SOX9+ cells do not co-express LHX2.

biological.citation: LHX2 Mediates the FGF-to-SHH Regulatory Loop during Limb Development (PMID: 29914077)
biological.summary: Transcriptome analysis of FGF-treated chick limb buds identified LHX2 as an intermediate in FGF-mediated regulation of SHH. LHX2 acts as a competency factor maintaining distal posterior SHH expression beneath the AER.

biological.citation: Lhx2 regulates bone remodeling in mice by modulating RANKL signaling in osteoclasts (PMID: 24902903)
biological.summary: Lhx2 is highly expressed in osteoclast precursors and falls during RANKL-induced osteoclastogenesis. Its overexpression inhibits NFATc1 induction. Lhx2 interacts with c-Fos, reducing c-Fos DNA binding and NFATc1 transactivation. Lhx2 conditional knockout mice show an osteoporotic phenotype with increased osteoclast formation.

biological.citation: Lhx2 mediates the activity of Six3 in zebrafish forebrain growth (PMID: 16226737)
biological.summary: In zebrafish, the telencephalon reduction in six3a/six3b morphants was fully rescued by head-specific lhx2 overexpression (caged mRNA), whereas Six3b could not rescue lhx2 knockdown. Lhx2 acts downstream of or parallel to Six3 in controlling forebrain progenitor proliferation.

biological.citation: MRG1 binds to the LIM domain of Lhx2 and may function as a coactivator to stimulate glycoprotein hormone alpha-subunit gene expression (PMID: 10593900)
biological.summary: A yeast two-hybrid screen identified MRG1 as an Lhx2 LIM-domain interactor, confirmed by in vitro binding and co-immunoprecipitation in alphaT3-1 cells. The Lhx2 LIM domain has intrinsic transactivation activity, and MRG1 enhances alpha-subunit reporter activity. MRG1 also binds TBP and p300, suggesting recruitment of p300/CBP and TBP.

biological.citation: LHX2- and LDB1-mediated trans interactions regulate olfactory receptor choice (PMID: 30626972)
biological.summary: LHX2 binds the Greek-island enhancers in mouse olfactory sensory neurons and works with the adaptor LDB1. Together they regulate interchromosomal olfactory receptor compartments, Greek island hubs, and olfactory receptor transcription.
